## Summary

A task's name and Goal can now be edited from the web page: the task view has an "Edit name and goal" button whose dialog saves through a new `/api/edit`, and the task's tree and log are left exactly as they were. In the terminal, `e` and the review editor now accept an `$EDITOR` with arguments such as `emacs -nw`, which failed before. Can't edit items

## Tree

### W11.1 · `tree.edit_task`: change a task's name and Goal in its file
Status: confirmed
Approach: In `scripts/tree.py` add `edit_task(task, name=None, goal=None)`: in the part that holds the Goal (`home_path`) rewrite the `# <task> · <name>` line and the text under `## Goal`, leaving the Tree and Log byte for byte as they were; ValueError for an empty name or a missing task. Tests in `scripts/test_tree.py`: name and Goal change, nodes and log are untouched, `check.py` still passes on the result.
Hypothesis: "Can't edit items" means the web page has no way to change a task's name or Goal after it is made (the terminal's `e` and the file itself can). Wrong if the author meant the terminal's `e` failing, or editing a node, which the history rule forbids. .dfs/artefacts/f711ba04-f3f4-4683-af19-eb834ee72363.html

- for: `web.py` routes `/api/title`, `/api/theme`, `/api/new`, `/api/answer` and node adds, and none rewrites an existing task's name or Goal.
- against: `tui.py` line `("items", "e", ... "edit the item's file in $EDITOR")` already edits an item, so the complaint may be about that path, which passes `$EDITOR` whole to `subprocess.call` so `EDITOR="emacs -nw"` fails.
- for: no web route or `tree.py` function changed a task's name or Goal before this node; the terminal path is covered by its own node, so either reading is met.
Determination: `tree.edit_task` rewrites the name and Goal and leaves the Tree and Log byte for byte (`test_tree.py` EditTask, 3 tests, whole file 68 pass).

### W11.2 · `POST /api/edit` on the web server
Parent: W11.1
Status: confirmed
Approach: In `scripts/web.py` add `edit_task(body)` for `name` and `goal` (the same size limits as `new_task`), under `LOCK`, calling `dfs_tree.edit_task`, then `HUB.notify()`; route it in `do_POST`. # W36 · Chat should have an interrupt button

## Summary

A chat on the page now has an Interrupt button, shown while the agent is answering. On a turn the page runs it ends the agent as ctrl-c would; on a chat the terminal screen runs in the background it types Esc, which stops the answer and drops any message still waiting to be typed. The conversation goes on with the next message, an interrupt that arrives just as a turn ends is refused rather than spoiling the next one, and each interrupt is written to the chat's log. The backend is covered by passing tests against stand-in agents; the button's page flow and Esc against a real claude could not be run here (no browser, no claude), so those are unseen.

## Goal

Chat should have an interrupt button

## Tree

### W36.1 · Interrupt a chat's answer in the backend
Status: confirmed
Approach: `chat.py`: `Chats.interrupt(scope)` stops what is answering. A headless page turn (`run_turn`) is tracked per scope and sent SIGTERM then SIGKILL after TURN_GRACE, as a timeout does, and its end is recorded as "Interrupted" rather than as a failure. A background chat (the screen's agent) is sent Esc, which claude takes as "stop this answer" without ending the session: `ptyrelay.Relay.interrupt()` writes `\x1b` to the pty and drops messages still queued to be typed; the walkers (`tui.py`, `walk.py` headless) get `chat_interrupt`. `web.py` gets `POST /api/chat/interrupt {scope}`, refusing when nothing is answering. Each interrupt is written to the chat's log. Check: unit tests in `test_chat.py`, `test_ptyrelay.py`, `test_web.py` (a slow stub turn is stopped and the chat accepts the next message; a fake agent on a pty receives Esc and queued text is dropped).
Determination: An interrupt stops a page-run turn (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL) and sends Esc to a screen-run chat that is answering, dropping its queued messages; the new tests pass, but Esc was tested against a stand-in agent, not a real claude.

### W36.2 · The button on the page
Parent: W36.1
Status: confirmed
Approach: `scripts/web/index.html`: an Interrupt button in the chat form, shown only while `st.busy`, posting `/api/chat/interrupt`; the Send button stays disabled meanwhile. README's chat paragraph gains a line. Check: a flow in `ui_flows.mjs` (playwright, if it runs here) shows the button while busy and none when idle; if no browser starts, say so.
Determination: The chat dialog shows an Interrupt button only while the agent is answering, and it posts to the new interrupt endpoint; the page flow and button are written but unrun here, since there is no browser or node in this environment, so the check that the button appears and works is still owed to a machine with playwright.

### W36.3 · Fix: a late interrupt leaves a stale `stopped` flag that kills the next turn
Parent: W36.1
Status: confirmed
Approach: In `scripts/chat.py` `Chats.turn`, the end of a turn takes `self.lock` twice: first to read and discard `scope` from `self.stopped` and pop `self.procs`, then (after `chatlog.log`, which does file IO) to pop `self.busy`. `Chats.interrupt` checks `scope in self.busy`, so an interrupt arriving between the two blocks passes the check, adds `scope` to `self.stopped` and returns success, though the turn is already over. Nothing clears that flag; the next `send` for the scope runs a turn whose `track()` sees `scope in self.stopped` and SIGTERMs the new agent at once, which then reports "Interrupted." with no answer. Fix: do the `stopped`/`procs` discard and the `busy` pop in one critical section (or have `interrupt` ignore a turn whose process has finished, and clear `stopped` when a turn begins in `send`). Add a test in `test_chat.py` that interrupts after the turn has read `stopped` but before `busy` is popped (e.g. by patching `chatlog.log` to call `interrupt`) and then checks that the next message is answered normally.
Determination: `Chats.turn` now discards `stopped`/`procs`, saves the session, sets the note and pops `busy` in one critical section, so an interrupt after that point is refused with "nothing is answering" and leaves no stale flag; the new test goes red on the old code and green on the new, and the other chat tests pass apart from the unrelated environmental failure.

### W36.4 · Minor findings from the review
Parent: W36.1
Status: confirmed
Approach:
- W36.1 rests on Esc stopping a real claude's answer without ending the session, tested only against a stand-in pty agent; its node has no `Hypothesis:` stating that assumption (what would refute it: a real claude that quits, opens a menu, or ignores Esc). Add one.
- W36.2's flow `chat_interrupt` in `ui_flows.mjs` and the button have never run (no browser here); run them where playwright exists.
- `test_chat.py::test_it_will_not_send_while_the_screens_chat_is_open_on_the_session` failed in this environment ("coreutils: unknown program 'claude ...'", `elsewhere` false); likely environmental and unrelated to W36, but confirm it passes on the base commit.
- After an interrupted first message, no session id is saved (the killed agent printed none), so the interrupted exchange is not part of the conversation; the page shows only "Interrupted.". Say so in the README line or keep the session id.
Determination: The README now says an interrupted first message leaves no session behind; the failing screen-chat test fails identically on the base commit, so it is environmental; the Hypothesis for W36.1 cannot be added to a node already confirmed, and the button flow still needs a machine with node and playwright, so those two stay unseen.

### W36.5 · Hypothesis: Esc stops a real claude's answer without ending the session or opening a menu
Parent: W36.1
Status: open
Approach: W36.1 (`ptyrelay.Relay.interrupt`, `Chats.interrupt` screen branch in `scripts/chat.py`) assumes that a lone `\x1b` written to a real claude's pty while it is answering (or has just been typed a message) stops that answer, leaves the session open for the next message, and opens no menu; and that Esc is only safe while answering because Esc twice at an idle prompt opens the rewind menu. It was tested only against a stand-in python pty agent in `test_ptyrelay.py`, never a real claude, and the node is confirmed with no `Hypothesis:` line, so the author does not see it. The first review also left it only in the `ok` text, and W36.4 could not add it to a confirmed node. State it as a `Hypothesis:` on this node with its page (what it rests on: claude's documented Esc-to-interrupt; what would refute it: a real claude that quits, opens a menu, ignores Esc, or treats `\x1b` followed by the later typed text as an Alt/escape sequence), and name the check owed: send a long question to a screen-run chat, press Interrupt, see the answer stop and a next message be answered. If the page-run side also rests on an unverified claim (a SIGTERMed `claude -p` prints no session id, so a first message leaves no session), state that under the same Hypothesis.

### W36.6 · Minor findings from the review
Parent: W36.1
Status: open
Approach:
- `README.md` (interrupt paragraph) says the page "shows only 'Interrupted.'" after an interrupted first message, but `Chats.pending` keeps the sent message shown beside it until the next send; reword.
- `index.html` shows the Interrupt button only while `st.busy`; for a screen chat with a message sent but not yet typed (`scope in pending`, agent not yet output) `busy` is false, though `Chats.interrupt` accepts that case. Either show the button then or drop the `pending` clause.

- `Chats.interrupt` calls `chatlog.log` (file IO) while holding the chats lock.

# W36 · Chat should have an interrupt button

## Summary

The chat dialog now shows an Interrupt button in place of Send while the agent is answering. It stops a turn the page runs itself, or types one Esc into a chat the terminal screen runs in the background and drops a message not yet typed; the conversation stays, the log shows an "Interrupted." note, and the next message goes on from it. The server side is covered by tests, but the page script and its browser flow could not be run here (no node, playwright or browser), and claude's reaction to the Esc was checked only against its documentation, not a live claude.

## Goal

Chat should have an interrupt button

## Tree

### W36.1 · Interrupt a turn the page runs itself
Status: confirmed
Approach: In `scripts/chat.py`, `run_turn` reports its `Popen` to the caller, and `Chats` keeps it per scope while the turn runs. New `Chats.interrupt(scope)` stops that process the way a timeout does (SIGTERM, SIGKILL after `TURN_GRACE`), also when the turn's thread has not started the process yet, and raises `ValueError("nothing to interrupt")` when the chat is not answering. The turn's thread then records a note "Interrupted." instead of the agent's exit as a failure, keeps the sent message shown, and frees the chat so the next message resumes the session. `web.py` serves it as `POST /api/chat/interrupt {scope}`. Checked in `test_chat.py` with a stub that sleeps (turn killed, no error text from the exit code, a second send works) and in `test_web.py` (the route, 409 when idle, 403 under `--no-walk`).
Determination: A turn the page runs is stopped by `Chats.interrupt` (also before its agent exists), ends as an "Interrupted." note rather than a failure, and the next message resumes; the new tests and the route test pass, while one older chat test (`exec -a` of the session id) fails here with or without the change.

### W36.2 · Interrupt a chat running in the screen's background
Parent: W36.1
Status: confirmed
Approach: `ptyrelay.Relay.interrupt()` drops the messages still queued in `outbox` and, when the agent is writing output, writes one ESC byte (0x1b) to the pty under `self.lock`, logs it, and returns whether it did anything. `walk.py`'s no-screen engine gets `chat_interrupt` returning False and `tui.py`'s engine forwards to the relay. `Chats.interrupt` uses it when the chat is live on the screen. Checked in `test_ptyrelay.py` with an agent that reads raw bytes, counts ESC and ignores nothing else (one ESC arrives, none when idle, the queue is dropped), and in `test_chat.py` with the fake screen.
Hypothesis: A single ESC byte written to the background claude's pty stops its current turn and keeps the session, as Esc does typed in a terminal. Wrong if a real claude keeps answering after the byte, or ends its session. .dfs/artefacts/a6cbb228-67d3-4418-a02f-2fd6b9949f24.html
Evidence:
- for: claude's interactive-mode documentation lists Esc as the key that interrupts a running operation, clears the input when nothing runs, and exits on a second press (code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode).
- against: none found; no claude binary exists in this session, so the Esc was only delivered to a stand-in agent on a pty, which shows the delivery and not claude's reaction.
Determination: `Relay.interrupt` types one Esc only while the agent is writing and drops what was queued or taken but not yet typed, `Chats.interrupt` hands a screen-run chat to it, and a stop shows as an "Interrupted." note; the tests pass and the documentation supports the hypothesis, which no live claude could be run against here.

### W36.3 · The Interrupt button on the chat page
Parent: W36.2
Status: confirmed
Approach: In `scripts/web/index.html` the chat form gets an Interrupt button beside Send, shown only while `st.busy`, which posts `/api/chat/interrupt` for the open scope and redraws from the returned state (a toast on refusal). A `ui_flows.mjs` chat flow with a slow stub agent presses it and sees Send enabled again with an "Interrupted." note. The README's chat paragraph and the `chat.py` docstring mention it.
Determination: While a chat is answering, Send gives way to Interrupt, which posts to the new route and shows a Stopping… line, then an Interrupted. note, and Send returns; the server side is tested, but the page script and the new `chatinterrupt` flow could not be run here (no node, playwright or browser), so they are read, not seen.

### W36.4 · Break it
Parent: W36.3
Status: confirmed
Approach: Try to break the work, clause by clause. Interrupt twice in a row. Interrupt with nothing running. Interrupt in the instant before the turn's process exists. Interrupt, then send, and check the session resumes and the transcript has no duplicate. Interrupt an opening turn. Interrupt a chat on `project`. Interrupt under `--no-walk`. Reload the page mid-turn and see the button. Each check is a test or a recorded run; the Determination says which failed, and what failed is fixed before the tree is complete.
Determination: Of the checks, interrupting twice, with nothing running, before the agent exists, an opening turn, the project chat, `--no-walk`, a stop that raced the answer, and interrupt-then-send (resumed once, message not repeated) all held in tests, and the screen engine's route to the relay was untested until now and passes; the browser side, a reload mid-turn and the 360px layout of the Interrupt button could not be run here (no node, playwright or browser), so the Goal is met on the server and in the page code as read, not as seen.

### W36.5 · Fix: Relay.interrupt types another Esc each time it is called while the agent still looks active
Parent: W36.2
Status: open
Approach: In `scripts/ptyrelay.py`, `Relay.interrupt()` writes ESC whenever `self.active` (output within the last 2 s). An agent that has just been stopped redraws ("Interrupted"), so it stays `active` for up to 2 s, and every further call in that window types one more Esc. Checked here with a throwaway script: a busy stand-in agent on a `Relay`, three `interrupt()` calls in a row returned True, True, True and the agent logged `ESC` three times (the existing test only calls it once, so "one Esc, not more" is not tested for repeats). Claude's interactive-mode docs list Esc+Esc at an empty prompt as the rewind menu (and at a prompt with text, clearing the draft), so a repeated Esc can leave a menu open that swallows the next message the page types, and the page cannot undo that. A repeat can really come from the page: `index.html`'s `#chat-stop` click handler disables the button, but `chatDraw` returns early on an unchanged signature and, when the signature changes while `busy` is still true (e.g. the transcript's new "[Request interrupted by user]" note), it sets `disabled = !!st.stopping`, which is false for a screen-run chat (`stopping` only exists for page-run turns), so the button is live again within the 2 s; a second tab or a double POST does the same. Fix: make a second interrupt of the same activity type no Esc: e.g. remember the time of the last Esc in `Relay` and send none until the agent has been quiet since (output gap after it, or a new message typed), and still drop the queue and return a truthy value so the page is not told "nothing is answering". Also keep the page's button disabled for a screen-run chat until `busy` goes false (or show a Stopping line from the relay's state). Settle it with a `test_ptyrelay.py` case calling `interrupt()` three times on the busy agent and asserting the agent logged exactly one ESC, and a `test_chat.py` case that a second `Chats.interrupt` on a screen-run chat does not reach the relay's pty twice. Correct the docstring of `Relay.interrupt` in the same change: it says a second Esc "would end" claude, but per the docs exit is Ctrl+C, and a second Esc opens the rewind menu or clears the draft.

Parent: W36.5
Status: open
Approach: Small things, one per line; none is a reason by itself.
- `chat.py` `stop()` repeats the SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL-after-`TURN_GRACE` logic that `run_turn`'s timeout path has; the two could share it.
- W36.2's Evidence ("exits on a second press") and the `Relay.interrupt` docstring mix up Esc and Ctrl+C; the docs say Ctrl+C exits on a second press, Esc+Esc rewinds or clears the draft.

- A screen-run chat shows no "Stopping…" line after Interrupt (`stopping` is only set for page-run turns), so the page shows nothing until the next poll.

# W36 · Chat should have an interrupt button

## Summary

The chat dialog has a Stop button that takes Send's place while the agent is answering. For a turn the page runs itself it ends the agent as ctrl-c would, keeps the conversation and shows an "Interrupted" line, so the next message resumes the same session. For the screen's background chat it types one Esc into that agent's terminal, and only while the agent is answering. The Goal is met in code; the browser flow for the button and a real claude's response to Esc were not run here (no browser and no claude installed), so the author should try both.

## Goal

Chat should have an interrupt button

## Tree

### W36.1 · Interrupt a turn the page runs itself
Status: confirmed
Approach: In `scripts/chat.py`, `run_turn` registers its `Popen` per scope (new `Chats.procs`); new `Chats.interrupt(scope)` terminates that process (SIGTERM, as ctrl-c ends it, SIGKILL after the existing grace), marks the scope interrupted so `turn()` records a quiet "Interrupted" note instead of an error and keeps the session id, and clears `busy` so the author can send again. A message queued to the screen's background chat is dispatched to `walker.chat_interrupt` (W36.2); with nothing answering it raises ValueError("nothing is answering"). Route `POST /api/chat/interrupt {scope}` in `scripts/web.py` `chat_act`. Check: `test_chat.py` with a stub claude that sleeps shows busy then not busy, the session id kept, an "Interrupted" note and no error, and that a following send resumes the session; `test_web.py` covers the route (409 when idle, 403 with `--no-walk`).
Determination: `Chats.interrupt` ends a page-run turn (SIGTERM, SIGKILL after the grace), keeps the session id, shows a quiet "Interrupted" note and frees the scope; `test_chat` interrupt test and the `test_web` route checks pass, and the one failing test (`exec -a` in the sandbox's coreutils) fails the same on the untouched tree.

### W36.2 · Interrupt the screen's background chat
Parent: W36.1
Status: confirmed
Approach: `Relay.interrupt()` in `scripts/ptyrelay.py` writes one Esc byte (`\x1b`) to the agent's pty, claude's own key for stopping the answer it is giving, and logs it through the chat's record; it does nothing unless the relay is live and `active`. `Walker.chat_interrupt(scope)` in `scripts/tui.py` calls it on the scope's relay and the no-screen `Walker` in `scripts/walk.py` returns False; `Chats.interrupt` uses it when `chat_live(scope)`. Check: `test_ptyrelay.py` runs a pty child that echoes what it reads and shows exactly one `\x1b` arrives, once, and none to a relay that is not active; `test_chat.py` shows the dispatch with a fake screen.
Hypothesis: A single Esc written to a live interactive claude's pty stops the answer it is giving and leaves the session running and ready for the next message. Wrong if, in a real claude, Esc is ignored while the agent is working, or ends the session, or (sent at an idle prompt) opens a menu that swallows the next message. .dfs/artefacts/6f0b3a52-8d41-4c7e-9a15-2e7c4b1d9f60.html
Evidence:
- for: Claude Code's interactive-mode docs and cheat sheets list Esc as the key that stops a response or tool run mid-way, keeping the conversation (e.g. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode); read, not run, since no `claude` is installed here.
- against: the same sources say Esc pressed twice on an empty prompt opens a rewind menu, so `Relay.interrupt` sends one Esc and only while the agent has written output in the last two seconds; a thinking agent that is silent for longer is refused, which the page shows as a refusal.
Determination: `Relay.interrupt` types one Esc only into a live, active relay (pty test sees exactly one `1b`; an idle relay receives nothing), `Walker.chat_interrupt` reaches it and `Chats.interrupt` dispatches to it (fake-screen test); that a real claude honours the Esc rests on its documentation and is unrun here.

### W36.3 · The Stop button on the chat dialog
Parent: W36.2
Status: confirmed
Approach: In `scripts/web/index.html`, the chat form gets a Stop button beside Send, shown (and Send hidden) while `st.busy`, which posts `/api/chat/interrupt` for `CHAT.scope`, toasts a refusal, and reloads the chat; the "Thinking…" line stays until the server says it is not busy. Parent: W36.1
Status: open
Approach: In `scripts/chat.py`, `Chats.turn` discards `self.stopped[scope]` in its first lock block (after the agent has ended) but pops `self.busy[scope]` only in its second lock block, with a `chatlog.log` and a possible `save_sid` between them. `Chats.interrupt` only checks `scope in self.busy`, so a Stop that lands in that gap adds `scope` to `stopped` after the discard and nothing ever removes it.
